title: Numeric boundary and resource integrity report
threat_model: Harness promises: (a) retained research evidence (receipts, lineage, reports) is replayed, cited and cross-language compared; (b) the Quine relay supervisor admits bounded child programs under strict resource limits. Malformed or adversarial inputs are in scope as accidental inputs; this is not a hostile multi-tenant boundary. Findings are numerical-integrity and resource-containment defects, not memory-safety issues.

severity_definitions.High: silently wrong numerical values can be retained in evidence without a backstop
severity_definitions.Medium: integrity or scope gaps with partial backstops, or evidence-pipeline false negatives
severity_definitions.Low: contained boundary overshoot with a fail-closed backstop, or latent traps
severity_definitions.no_critical_note: No Critical assigned; no memory unsafety or remote exploitability was found.

findings.title: log chain gradient: avoidable intermediate overflow
findings.class: boundary computation: materializes 1/value before multiplying; overflows for subnormal-scale arguments although the exact derivative is finite
findings.impact: Programs using log on subnormal-scale inputs recorded nonfinite gradients beside a structural certificate; optimizers and boundary decisions could be misled. No memory unsafety.
findings.evidence: f(x)=log((1/1024)*x) at x=2^-1020: old derivative 1/(2^-1030) * 2^-10 = inf; exact derivative 2^1020 is finite binary64; C model reproduced overflow in three of five cases.
findings.fix: log@2 registered (direct division of each incoming derivative), domain refusal for value <= 0; parser resolves the active version through the single registry; legacy log@1 retained for replay.
findings.verification: operation::tests 3/3 (incl. log_v2_divides_before_an_avoidable_reciprocal_overflow); numeric_boundary 3/3 debug + 3/3 release; diagnostic v1/v2 emitted; upstream workspace 229 passed.

findings.title: Rational to f64: double-rounded operands cross the unit boundary
findings.class: boundary crossing: numerator and denominator cast to f64 separately before division; nearest conversion of the exact ratio not guaranteed
findings.impact: 9007199254740992/9007199254740993 evaluated to exactly 1.0 (bits 3ff0000000000000) although the nearest binary64 is one ulp below; values near the unit boundary silently wrong in evaluated programs and retainable in receipts.
findings.evidence: audit C model and native diagnostic v1/v2; old bits 3ff0000000000000 vs nearest 3fefffffffffffff; second case (2^53+1)/(2^53+2) erred the other direction by one ulp.
findings.fix: ade4f88 rewrites as_f64 with integer quotient/remainder arithmetic: round the exact ratio once to binary64, nearest with ties to even.
findings.verification: crates/adva-ir/tests/numeric_rounding.rs + numeric_json.rs (cargo test -p adva-ir 2/2 locally); pytest Fraction oracle over 2^53-boundary pairs and random i64 pairs (upstream 1637/2382 passed).

findings.title: Finite-value policy gap across APIs
findings.class: boundary-policy gap: NaN and positive infinity accepted as inputs; nonfinite outputs could serialize as null beside a structural certificate
findings.impact: Structural certificates did not over-claim numerical truth, but callers could not obtain a finite-only guarantee; serializers could emit null beside a certificate.
findings.evidence: FINDINGS.md item 3: Python KernelFunction._check_inputs accepted NaN/inf; log guard value <= 0.0 is false for NaN.
findings.fix: evaluate_finite and evaluate_with_finite_differential entry points (explicit finite-input/output/Jacobian scope in the certificate); numeric_serialization.rs refuses nonfinite values and Jacobian entries; native run refuses nonfinite outputs and log domain failures.
findings.verification: native_run_refuses_nonfinite_outputs_and_log_domain_failures; pytest test_nonfinite refusals at public and direct native entry points; serialization refusal tests.
findings.status: Fixed (ade4f88); intermediate values and unused differentials remain out of the certified scope (documented).

findings.title: Quine relay: sub-second CPU remainder expanded to one full second
findings.class: the Xe round_up class verbatim: max(1, min(child_limit, floor(remaining))) rounds a fractional remainder outward across the budget boundary
findings.impact: With 0.25s aggregate remainder the child limit became 1s; post-hoc check() rejection held (no overspent run accepted), but the harness could not promise a strict pre-execution aggregate bound.
findings.evidence: FINDINGS.md item 4 with mocked setrlimit at remainders 0, 0.25, nextafter(1,0), 1, 1.25, 2, 8.75.
findings.fix: child_cpu_limit(): admit only a whole-second limit contained in both the per-child cap and the aggregate remainder; refuse before recording, opening files or forking.
findings.verification: test_quine_cpu_budget.py 6/6 locally and upstream; AEG ported suite 6/6.
findings.status: Fixed (61a7ae4); further hardened by F-5 fix.

findings.title: Quine relay: child recomputed the allowance after fork
findings.class: boundary recomputed on the wrong side of fork: the child's RUSAGE_CHILDREN is zero, so remaining = budget + start could inflate the installed limit
findings.impact: The child could install an RLIMIT_CPU larger than the allowance the parent admitted; identified during fix review of F-4 before it shipped in a release beyond 61a7ae4's merged state.
findings.evidence: review of preexec_fn semantics: getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN) in a fresh child returns zero.
findings.fix: restrictions(cpu) installs the parent-precomputed allowance via functools.partial; the child never reads its own child accounting.
findings.verification: test_parent_allowance_is_installed_without_reading_child_accounting (fork mock asserts child_cpu raises if consulted); AEG ported suite 6/6.

findings.title: k28 JSON transport: serde_json default formatting lost one ulp
findings.location: crates/adva-witness native run report serialization (serde_json without float_roundtrip)
findings.class: cross-language evidence transport precision loss at the JSON boundary
findings.impact: The native report echoed y = 0.9999999962747096 (0x3feffffffdffffff) for a submitted 0.9999999962747097 (0x3feffffffe000000 = 1 - 2^-28); the Python exact-Fraction matcher rejected product-k28 (false negative in the research 0141 suite).
findings.fix: workspace serde_json feature float_roundtrip (ade4f88); regression test native_input_and_report_preserve_k28_binary64_values.
findings.verification: regression test passed locally; replay of the retained program through the current backend reports exact bits and values [1.0] with echoed inputs equal to the submitted JSON.
findings.status: Fixed (ade4f88); closure record 4a881d7 on research/k28-json-transport-closure (not yet merged).

findings.title: AEG calibration: float ceil(log) on an integral boundary
findings.class: boundary exactly on the cell edge computed in binary64: ceil(log2(1024 + ulp)) computed 10 while the true minimum is 11
findings.impact: Correct by luck for the current constants (log2(1024) = 10.0 exactly); a one-ulp displacement of the constants would flip m, and the independent hard-coded check would convert a true proposition into Rejected (false negative).
findings.evidence: demonstrated at 2^10 + 1 ulp: old formula 10, exact loop 11.
findings.fix: AEG 62bced8: count shrink steps with exact Fraction arithmetic; archived report.json unchanged.
findings.verification: rerun JSON-equal to the archived report; boundary comparison script.

findings.title: AEG merge demo: norm() round-trips numbers through float
findings.location: AEG .merge-two-sides.py norm(): int(value) if float(value).is_integer() else float(value)
findings.class: same trap as F-2 at the harness level: values above 2^53 collapse to distinct floats
findings.impact: Demonstration values (14) are safe; the rule is latent for any future integer beyond 2^53.

not_found: No floating-point-to-allocation-size path analogous to the Xe VRAM allocator bug.
No silent acceptance of an overspent budget run; post-hoc checks held in every case.
No certificate found to over-claim exact numerical truth beyond its declared scope.
No memory unsafety or remote exploitability.
residual_open_items: Intermediate values and unused differentials are not certified finite (documented certificate scope).
No rounding-error bound for arbitrary programs; log@2 removes the avoidable overflow, not every last-bit difference.
toolchain-watch.json historical fields are pre-merge snapshots; post-merge state recorded in merge_refresh_20260910 (commit 60b37d8, on origin/main).
k28 closure record on research/k28-json-transport-closure (4a881d7) not yet merged.

methodology_checklist: Boundary-direction questions: what lies below/above the line; does rounding contract (inward) or expand (outward) the safe region; is the assertion derived from the same logic it checks?
Independent oracles: exact Fractions, bit patterns, power-of-two expectations.
Model first, native second: C scalar model reproduces the defect, then native replay gates the fix.
Bit-pattern replay at every transport boundary (parse and serialize both sides; compare to_bits).
Frozen baselines: retained evidence is never relabeled; audit scripts refuse to run against drifted source.
Versioned fixes: register the corrected rule as a new version; legacy replay stays executable.
Native acceptance gate order: fmt -> clippy -> debug/release tests -> examples -> extension build -> full pytest.
Toolchain defect watch: MSRV/CI inventory with triage records.
boundaries: Single-repository evidence-grade audit, not a third-party security audit. No universal numerical-safety claim, no rounding-error bound for arbitrary programs, and no claim of exact OS CPU accounting. Original retained reports and library evidence were not regenerated.
